listeners.text: Late night shift... just a handful of us locked in right now. Pure focus.
Room's filling up nicely... shout to the crew locking in from across the globe.
Dozens of heads in the room right now sharing this frequency. Big love to every single one of you.
Wherever you're listening from tonight—headphones, car speakers, bedroom—we're all in this room together.

intro.text: Delilah Montagu singing straight out of her kitchen into an iPhone memo. Fred caught the feeling while waiting on his laundry. Hold tight... here it comes.

thought.text: Fred kept the actual phone hiss on Delilah's vocal. Most producers would scrub it clean. That imperfection is the magic.

outro.text: Delilah, pulling us all out of this. Unbelievable energy.

intro.text: Danielle Balbuena, 070 Shake on the vocal. That raw acoustic emotion wrapped in pure club euphoria.

thought.text: You can hear the raw ache in 070 Shake's voice... but Fred wraps it in chords that make you want to dance through it.

outro.text: Danielle, smile on my face. That smile is now permanent.

intro.text: The very first breath of the Actual Life journey. Nathan's words, caught in transit, reminding us all to just keep going.

thought.text: Nathan's voice note was recorded on a curb in Atlanta. That simple reminder to keep breathing carries the whole album.

outro.text: Nathan, still breathing. The heartbeat of the archive.

intro.text: Kammy Purcell on the vocal. Fred pitched down her acapella from an Instagram video while riding the Eurostar. Pure warmth.

thought.text: Kammy's vocal was an offhand Instagram freestyle. Fred slowed it down on a train and built a sanctuary around it.

intro.text: Tanya. Only on the record does the name get a second half. Turn this one up.

thought.text: Tanya's words "maybe life"... it's that feeling when you're not sure where things are going, but you let the beat carry you anyway.

intro.text: Pangbourne crew in full effect. Skrillex, Flowdan, and Fred. Four years in the making. Watch the low end on this drop.

thought.text: Three days in the countryside tweaking that one modular sub-bass. You don't just hear this track, you feel it in your ribs.

outro.text: Flowdan and Skrillex with Fred. Heavyweight pressure.

intro.text: Written during those legendary countryside sessions with Skrillex and Four Tet. Turn the lights out for this one.

thought.text: Four Tet, Skrillex, and Fred jamming in a living room at 4 AM. That playful friendship is baked into every kick drum.

intro.text: Future, Swedish House Mafia, and Fred. Studio sound welded to the rave.

thought.text: Future's vocals echoing like they're coming from the back room of a warehouse rave. Unstoppable momentum.

intro.text: Dense, relentless energy. Fred wrote this to break the sound system. Here we go.

thought.text: Listen to the way the percussion rolls over itself. Pure London sound-system pressure.

intro.text: Obongjayar's voice arrives and the whole track opens up. Dedicated to his sister. Beautiful feeling right here.

thought.text: Obongjayar singing to his little sister. In the middle of a massive festival, it turns into an intimate prayer.

intro.text: The final chapter of the Boiler Room. The night is dark and the name is Clara.

thought.text: The final track from the Boiler Room. Clara's voice guiding everyone through the dark and out the other side.

intro.text: Built from something fragile. Romy and Fred letting the chords hold the entire room.

thought.text: Romy's voice is so gentle here. It takes real courage to make dance music that feels this tender.
That voice note at the end of Kyle... "I found you". It's the moment you realize you're going to be alright.

intro.text: A little lift in the room. Let this one open the windows.
All that pressure, all that release. Keep your eyes on the low end.
No rush to leave this moment. Stay in it with us.
A voice like a hand on your shoulder. Here's Billie.
For the ones finding their way through. This is Carlos.
Different streets, same shared pulse. Lock into this one.
Lift off from here. Flight FM, on Again Radio.
For the late shift and the long way home. Here's Nightvision.

boiler-room-london.text: Stepping into the iconic London Boiler Room. Sweat on the walls, pure electricity.

rooftop-naples.text: Heading over to Naples on that sun-drenched terrace. Golden hour over the sea.

times-square.text: Times Square, New York City. A yellow school bus and three friends stopping traffic.

tiny-desk.text: NPR Tiny Desk. No backing tracks, just classical piano, marimba, and live MPC loops.

facts.text: Fred knocked on Brian Eno's door at sixteen and joined his acapella group. Eno mentored him for over a decade before they made Secret Life together.
Every name in Fred's titles is a real person he met. The voice notes on his phone become the emotional soul of the music.
Before releasing solo records, Fred produced massive chart-toppers for Ed Sheeran, George Ezra, and Stormzy on his laptop.
During the 2022 Boiler Room, a dancer bumped the CDJ stop button. Fred just grinned, hit play, and turned it into the defining moment of the set.
